- If sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) or neutral, model often underestimates; increase forecast to reflect potential rebound.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model frequently overcorrects downward; delay or reduce downward adjustment.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: if price has been trending sharply, forecast often pulls back too early; allow for lingering momentum.
- For 30-day horizon, model underestimates true price volatility in high-sentiment periods; add 1–2% buffer to forecast if sentiment >0.67.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag in direction; align forecast with sentiment swing midpoint rather than trend end.
